title: Record the c=1 stabilizer action outside the {g,t} normalizer.
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Exhaustive finite census for one joint eigenspace of the historical doubled centre block at `c=1`. The trivial sign character splits into four 216-dimensional joint spaces under the involutions `g` and `t`. Inside the `c=1` stabilizer of order 3072, the setwise stabilizer of the trivial-character `(+1,+1)` space has order 768. The normalizer of `{1,g,t,gt}` has order 96 and sits inside that setwise stabilizer.

Of the 672 preservers outside the normalizer, 560 act non-scalarly on the 216-space. The kernel of the setwise stabilizer has order 64, so its image in `GL(E)` has order 12 and equals the dihedral image already produced by the normalizer. These elements are further lifts of those twelve operators. They do not cut a finer `A_1`-invariant subspace than PR #7008.

One witness is the involution `w` with permutation `(4 7)(5 6)` and a minus sign only on coordinate 1. It is the normalizer involution `u` multiplied by the coordinate-1 sign. That sign acts by `+I` on the 216-space, so `w` and `u` have the same trace 72 there. The coordinate-1 sign does not normalize the Klein group, and neither does `w`.

No new kappa. The selected conditional kappa stays `781451/250000000`.

Evidence class: exhaustive finite census of a finite set of order 3072, plus one constructive witness. The completeness argument is the decomposition of the hyperoctahedral group into 30 left cosets of the line-preserving subgroup. This is not a heuristic search and not an unrestricted nonexistence claim.

## Task and overlap

- Task: `formal-interface-lemma`, scope changed.
- Upstream base: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840` (priority revision 8).
- Assigned question: does any signed permutation in the `c=1` stabilizer, outside the normalizer of `{g,t}`, preserve the trivial-character `(+1,+1)` 216-space and act non-scalarly?
- Predecessor: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7008
- Finding being answered: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19507672
- Package: `research/c1-216-outside-normalizer/`

The catalogue card asks for a formal caller binding. PR #7008 proves reducibility of this 216-space under its signed normalizer and leaves the outside-normalizer question open. Its stored second question is worded for the 8-dimensional isotypic summand. This package answers the 216-dimensional preservation question. It does not decide irreducibility of that 8-dimensional summand under `A_1`, and it does not take the 48-dimensional eigenspaces of PR #7009 or the settled `c=3` sign split of PR #6965.

Overlap on 2026-11-10 against `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`: local notes 10178 of 10178, complete; 317 open PRs, pagination complete, fetched 2026-11-10T08:49:45Z; 6971 discussion records, pagination complete, fetched 2026-11-10T08:50:46Z. The phrases `216-dimensional summand`, `non-scalarly`, and `normalizer of` match #7008 and discussion comment 19507672, which ask the question, and the local notes for the `c=3` split and the original sign split, which are different blocks. No open PR reports this 768-element stabilizer. Closed PRs were searched through local READMEs, task metadata, and the ledger only. No code diffs.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only. Both modes passed. Metadata check returned `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. Selected baseline returned `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.

```sh
python3 -B -W error research/c1-216-outside-normalizer/verify.py
python3 -B -O research/c1-216-outside-normalizer/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/c1-216-outside-normalizer --check-only
```

Marker: `PASS_C1_216_OUTSIDE_NORMALIZER`.

The line-preserving signed-permutation group has order 344064 and index 30 in the hyperoctahedral group. The `c=1` stabilizer has order 3072. Preserver trace histogram: `216: 64`, `-216: 64`, `72: 192`, `-72: 192`, `24: 128`, `-24: 128`. Every projector correlation on the stabilizer is `0` or `216`. Rejection controls cover a coordinate transposition, the incomplete swap of coordinates 4 and 7, a swapped port label, a projector sum that drops `g`, the normalizer element `u`, and the coordinate-1 sign that preserves the space but acts by `+I`.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the degree-881 replay, any characteristic polynomial, and the selected cold replay.

## Credit

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance.

JoyboyBrian recorded the sign-character dimensions. PR #6944 split the trivial `c=1` character into 216-dimensional blocks. PR #7008 computed the normalizer and the dihedral image of order 12. Ali Romman's PR4958 and PR4720 retain the query and the Bell action. Krzysztof Wojt's `research/exact-one-slot-gram/` supplies the 13 generators and the degree-881 annihilator. Nick Petalas's PR5120 is the degree-410 lower bound. The doubled representation comes from PR1719. New work is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

See `research/c1-216-outside-normalizer/TASK.json`.

- Does any `c=1` stabilizer element that moves the 216-space preserve the 8-dimensional dihedral isotypic summand and act non-scalarly on it? Under the linear-character identification in #7008, elements that preserve the 216-space act by scalars on that summand. The trace on the 4096-dimensional block does not decide an element that moves the space.
- Is the 8-dimensional isotypic summand irreducible under `A_1`? This census does not build its basis.
